spec.title: Task progress indicator in sidebar
spec.context: When viewing the sidebar kanban, there is no way to see how far along a task's implementation is without opening the plan.xml file. Users have to click into each task to check progress, which breaks their flow and slows down board scanning. Adding an at-a-glance progress indicator reduces context-switching and helps users quickly identify which tasks are nearly done, just started, or where to focus.

in-scope.item: Parse plan.xml to count completed vs total tasks
Display progress as "3/7" in TaskItem description
Auto-refresh when plan.xml changes (via existing file watcher)
Show progress in tooltip as well

out-of-scope.item: Progress bar or graphical indicator (text fraction is sufficient)

requirements.requirement: The plan-parser computer shall expose a getPlanProgress function that accepts plan.xml content and returns completed count and total count of tasks
The tasks orchestrator shall read plan.xml content for each task that has one, and pass progress data to the view capability
The TaskItem description shall display progress as "completed/total" (e.g., "3/7") after the file indicators and before the next action arrow
When a task has no plan.xml, no progress indicator shall be shown
When a plan.xml file is modified, the existing file watcher shall trigger a tree refresh that updates progress counts
The TaskItem tooltip shall include progress information when available

file.reason: Add getPlanProgress function to count completed/total tasks
Accept progress data in TaskItem, display in description and tooltip
Wire plan.xml reading to pass progress data to view capability

pattern.name: Computer Factory
pattern.description: Pure functions wrapped in factory. getPlanProgress will be added to createPlanParserComputer return type alongside parsePlanSymbols.

pattern.name: Dependency Injection via Deps
pattern.description: TasksViewCapabilityDeps interface defines injected functions. A new getPlanProgress dep will be added following the same pattern as checkTaskFiles.

pattern.name: Description Parts Array
pattern.description: TaskItem.buildDescription() builds description by pushing strings to a parts array and joining with space. Progress indicator follows this pattern.

product.finding: Sidebar TreeView already has auto-refresh via file watcher on tasks/**/*.xml. Shows priority, labels, file indicators, and next action in description.
Implement skill marks tasks completed="true" in plan.xml - this is the data source for progress counting.

engineering.finding: No engineering docs found, but codebase follows computer/capability/orchestrator architecture consistently.

codebase.finding: Already parses plan.xml task elements and reads completed attribute. Can be extended with a lightweight progress counting function reusing the same XMLParser instance.
TaskItem.buildDescription() at line 69 builds description with parts array. Progress indicator slots in after file indicators (line 97) and before next action (line 101).
Wires all dependencies. Already reads plan.xml existence via checkTaskFiles. Would add plan content reading and progress computation.

pitfall.mitigation: Existing watcher at tasks.orchestrator.ts:332 watches tasks/**/*.xml which includes plan.xml. No new watcher needed.
Each refresh reads plan.xml for tasks that have one. Files are small XML, read synchronously, minimal impact.

constraints.constraint: Must use ThemeIcons and ThemeColors only (design directive)
All exported functions must have explicit return types and TSDoc

dependencies.dependency: Existing file watcher infrastructure in tasks orchestrator

risk.mitigation: Plan files are small; synchronous reads are fast

risks.risk: Slightly increased I/O on each tree refresh due to reading plan.xml files
